\chapter{Communication Complexity — Func Hash}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.FuncHash
\section{Overview}

This module establishes a key probabilistic lemma for Newman's theorem: a uniformly
random hash function $h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ collides on any two distinct
inputs with probability at most $1/k$.  The argument proceeds by decomposing the
collision event into $k$ pairwise-disjoint pieces, measuring each piece, and summing.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Hash function space]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch03-randomized-protocols}{pdf-3eebfb23ab53-p001-b002}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace}
\leanok
$\texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k$ is the type of all functions $\alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$,
i.e.\ the space of hash functions on $\alpha$ with output range $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$.
Equipped with the product probability measure (uniform over each coordinate), it serves
as the ambient probability space for the random-hash argument.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Collision piece]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace}
For $x, y : \alpha$ and $a : \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, $\texttt{collisionPiece}\,k\,x\,y\,a$ is
the set of hash functions $h \in \texttt{HashSpace}\,\alpha\,k$ satisfying $h(x) = a$ and
$h(y) = a$, i.e.\ the subset of the product space where both $x$ and $y$ are mapped to
the fixed value $a$.  These pieces partition the collision event $\{h \mid h(x) = h(y)\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Collision event as a union of collision pieces]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collision_mem_iUnion}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collision_mem_iUnion}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.HashSpace, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $k$ be a natural number, and let $x, y \in \alpha$. Writing
a hash function as a map $h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, the collision event on which
$x$ and $y$ receive the same hash value decomposes as the union of collision pieces over
all possible common values:
\[
  \{\, h : \alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k \mid h(x) = h(y) \,\}
  \;=\; \bigcup_{a \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k} \{\, h \mid h(x) = a \text{ and } h(y) = a \,\}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Pairwise disjointness of the collision pieces]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_pairwiseDisjoint}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_pairwiseDisjoint}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a type $\alpha$, a natural number $k$, and two elements $x, y : \alpha$. For each
value $a \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, let $C_a$ denote the set of hash functions $h : \alpha
\to \{0, \dots, k-1\}$ with $h(x) = a$ and $h(y) = a$. Then the family $(C_a)_a$ is
pairwise disjoint: whenever $a \ne b$, the sets $C_a$ and $C_b$ have empty intersection.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Volume of a singleton in a finite type]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measure}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measure}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
Let $k \ge 1$ be a natural number and let $a$ be an element of the finite type
$\mathrm{Fin}\,k = \{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}$, equipped with its canonical (uniform) volume
measure. Then the measure of the singleton $\{a\}$ equals $1/k$, as an element of the
extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform measure of a singleton in a finite type]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measureReal}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measureReal}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measure}
\difficulty{2}
Let $k \ge 1$, and equip the finite set $\mathrm{Fin}\,k = \{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}$ with
its uniform probability measure. Then for every element $a \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, the
real-valued measure of the singleton $\{a\}$ equals $1/k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Measure of a collision piece]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_measureReal}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece_measureReal}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_pi_univ, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.collisionPiece, CommunicationComplexity.Functions.Hash.hashRange_singleton_measureReal}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $k \ge 1$. Fix two distinct elements $x \ne y$ of
$\alpha$ and a value $a \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, and equip the space of hash functions
$\alpha \to \mathrm{Fin}\,k$ with the product of the uniform probability measures on the
coordinates. Then the collision piece consisting of those hash functions $h$ with $h(x)
= a$ and $h(y) = a$ has measure
\[
  \left(\frac{1}{k}\right)^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{4}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $k \ge 1$, so that each hash value lies in
$\{0,\dots,k-1\}$. Consider the space of hash functions $h \colon \alpha \to
\mathrm{Fin}\,k$, equipped with the uniform product probability measure, and fix two
distinct points $x \ne y$ in $\alpha$. Then the probability that $x$ and $y$ collide is
at most $1/k$:
\[
  \Pr\bigl[\,h(x) = h(y)\,\bigr] \;\le\; \frac{1}{k}.
\]
\end{theorem}
